title: Equivariant elliptic cohomology via loop spaces
abstract:
We construct a cohomology theory $H_A(-)$ canonically attached to any 1-dimensional commutative group scheme A over a connective $E_\infty$-ring. The additive group in characteristic zero gives 2-periodic de Rham cohomology, the multiplicative group gives topological periodic cyclic homology, and an elliptic curve gives elliptic cohomology. The construction extends to the G-equivariant setting for an algebraic group G, yielding in the elliptic case a theory of equivariant elliptic cohomology on algebraic varieties with G-action that takes values in sheaves on the stack of G-bundles. Over the complex numbers, and for G connected reductive, this lifts Grojnowski's theory from the moduli space of G-bundles to the stack.
  The key player is the category of perfect complexes on A with 0-dimensional support, equipped with the convolution product induced by the group law of A. It plays the role of a categorified circle and is used to define a loop space $L_A^G(X)$, whose structure sheaf gives rise to $H_A^G(X)$ after periodization. Sheaves on $L_A^G(X)$ equivariant under loop rotation provide a category of coefficients for $H_A^G(-)$ in the same way that D-modules provide coefficients for de Rham cohomology. At the point X = *, the theory also gives rise to an $E_\infty$-ring spectrum (or sheaf thereof) $K_A$, which recovers complex K-theory for $A = \mathbf{G}_m$, and the sheaf $\mathcal{O}^{top}$ of topological modular forms for the universal elliptic curve.

title: On Diameter Graphs Problems: A proof of Brass's Conjecture
abstract:
The diameter graph of a finite set $S\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ has vertex set $S$ and two points are adjacent when their distance equals $\operatorname{diam} S$. In this paper we study the following question: given $k$ and $d$, is there a constant $c=c(k,d)$ such that from every finite point set $S\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ one can remove at most $c$ points so that the subgraph of the diameter graph induced by the remaining points is $k$-colorable? Brass conjectured that such a constant exists for $d=3$ and $k=3$. We prove this conjecture by showing that at most one point needs to be removed.
  We also answer a question of Dol'nikov, showing that for every positive integer $m$, there exist a finite point set $S\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ in which every subset of smaller diameter has less than $(|S|-m)/2$ points.

title: Almost All 3-uniform Hypergraphs are Class 1
abstract: The chromatic index $χ'(H)$ of a hypergraph $H$ is the smallest number of colors needed to color its edges so that no two adjacent edges share the same color. The chromatic index is trivially bounded below by the maximum degree $Δ(H)$, and when $χ'(H)= Δ(H)$, we say that $H$ is Class 1. It is well known that almost every 2-graph is Class 1, and we extend this result to 3-graphs. We show for $n^{-2/3-1/200}\leq p \leq 0.99$ that the $3$-uniform binomial random hypergraph $H\sim H_{n,p}^{(3)}$ is Class 1 with high probability. We also show that this result doesn't hold for uniformities above $3$. For a broad range of $p$, when $k \geq 4$ and $k \nmid n$, the hypergraph $H \sim H_{n,p}^{(k)}$ is with high probability not Class 1.

title: On the most informative Boolean function under noise
abstract: Let $X$ be a uniform random bit string and $Y$ be obtained by flipping each bit of $X$ independently with probability $p$. Let $C$ be a random bit obtained as a function of $Y$. We show that $\mathbf{I}(C:X)\le \mathbf{I}(Y_1:X)$ for all $p\in[0,1]$, which resolves a conjecture posed by Courtade and Kumar in 2013.

title: Logarithmically Slim Polygons
abstract:
We study the relationship between the large-scale geometry of a geodesic metric space and the slimness of its geodesic polygons. We show that if there is a uniform constant $δ$ such that every geodesic polygon in an unbounded geodesic metric space is $δ$-slim, then the space has asymptotic Assouad--Nagata dimension one.
  We further consider graphs of bounded valency and allow the slimness constant of an $n$-gon to grow logarithmically with $n$. More precisely, under an explicit logarithmic bound on the slimness of geodesic $n$-gons, we prove that the graph has asymptotic Assouad--Nagata dimension one. Thus, sufficiently strong logarithmic control on the slimness of geodesic polygons forces one-dimensional large-scale geometry.
  We also obtain two criteria for graphs, outside the hyperbolic setting, to have asymptotic Assouad--Nagata dimension one. In particular, these criteria show that one-dimensional large-scale geometry can be detected from quantitative restrictions on the slimness of geodesic polygons, without requiring the space to be hyperbolic.

title: Homogeneous Polynomial Carleson Operators Along the Paraboloid
abstract: In this paper, we prove boundedness on $L^p(\mathbb{R}^{n+1})$, $1<p<\infty$, of polynomial Carleson operators along the paraboloid with phase belonging to a class $Y$ of homogeneous polynomials. For $n,d\ge 2$, let $\mathcal{P}^{n,d}$ denote the class of all real-valued homogeneous polynomials in $n$ variables of degree $d$. We may take the class $Y$ to be an arbitrary linear subspace $Y \subseteq \mathcal{P}^{n,d}$ such that $\dim Y \le M_{n , d}$, where $M_{n , d}$ is a constant depending only on $n$ and $d$. The main novelty of our result is that we may allow a large collection of homogeneous polynomials of the same degree, in contrast to earlier results that relied on distinct degree assumptions. The heart of our proof is a $TT^*$ method, and the derivation of new estimates for oscillatory integral kernels involving interactions between homogeneous polynomial phases and the paraboloid.

title: Dimensionally absolutely stable but non-diagonalizable $T$-meshes
abstract: We construct an infinite family of rectangular \(T\)-meshes whose conformality-vector-space dimension is constant over all structurally similar geometric realizations, although the meshes are not diagonalizable. For every integer \(d\ge 2\), the construction has \(2(d+2)\) \(\Tl\)-edges and intersection graph \(K_{d+2,d+2}\). Every \(\Tl\)-edge contains at least \(d+2\) vertices, so no edge is vanishable under the usual vertex-count criterion for bidegree \((d,d)\) and smoothness \((d-1,d-1)\). We prove that the conformality-vector space is one-dimensional throughout the structural similarity class. Its generator is the outer product of two vectors of barycentric interpolation weights, extended by four zero coordinates. Non-diagonalizability follows by examining the last edge in any proposed diagonalizing ordering. Thus, for the geometric structural similarity class specified here, diagonalizability is not a necessary condition for dimensional absolute stability.

title: Uniform comparison of multiplier and test ideals for polynomials with affinely independent support
abstract: Let $f\in\Q[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ have affinely independent exponent vectors. We prove that its test ideals agree with the reductions of its multiplier ideals at all nonnegative real exponents for every sufficiently large prime in one arithmetic progression. The progression depends only on the support of $f$.

title: Holomorphic flexibility properties of strongly commuting varieties
abstract: We study holomorphic flexibility properties of the strongly commuting variety of a complex semisimple algebraic group $G$. We prove that the smooth locus of the strongly commuting variety of $G$ is Oka-$1$. We also prove that the smooth locus of the commuting variety of a semisimple complex Lie algebra is Oka-$1$, and that it contains a Zariski dense open subset which is algebraically elliptic.

title: Large orbits of $p$-groups on conjugacy classes
abstract: Let $P$ be a $p$-group that acts faithfully and coprimely on a finite group $H$. A classical result of D.\ S.\ Passman, in the form proved by I.\ M.\ Isaacs, asserts that there exists an element $x\in H$ such that $|C_P(x)|\le (|P|/p)^{1/p}$. In this paper, we study the corresponding question for the action of $P$ on the conjugacy classes of $H$. We show that for every odd prime $p$ the analogue of Isaacs' bound fails for classes. On the other hand, we prove that if $H$ is solvable, then there always exists a conjugacy class $c$ of $H$ whose stabilizer in $P$ has order at most $|P|^{1/2}$, and that this bound is best possible for every prime $p$. As a consequence, there always exists an irreducible character of $H$ whose inertia group in $P$ has order at most $|P|^{1/2}$. The proof proceeds via a result on linear actions of $p$-nilpotent groups, and in the quasiprimitive case it relies on a classification of Holt and Yang and on computer calculations.

title: A sharp Bernstein theorem for affine maximal type surfaces
abstract: We investigate Bernstein theorem for the affine maximal type equation \begin{equation*} \sum_{i,j=1}^nf^{ij}(D^a)_{ij}=0,\qquad D=\det(f_{ij}),\qquad a\neq0, \end{equation*} under completeness of the Calabi metric. In dimension two, we prove that every smooth strictly convex solution on a convex domain is a quadratic polynomial whenever $a\notin[-\tfrac23,-\tfrac13]$, resolving a conjecture of Sun and Xu [25]. For every $n\geq2$, we also construct explicit non-quadratic Calabi complete solutions on convex domains for all $a\in[-\tfrac n{n+1},-\tfrac1{n+1}]$. These examples show that the rigidity range is sharp in dimension two.

title: Sharp Hausdorff--Young inequalities for some locally compact quantum groups
abstract: In this paper, we show that the usual Hausdorff--Young inequalities for locally compact quantum groups such as the quantum \(E_q(2)\), the real quantum \(az+b\), and the extended quantum \(SU_q(1,1)\), where \(0<q<1\), are sharp. Moreover, there are no group-like projections with finite Haar weight in these locally compact quantum groups. We obtain a sharp Hausdorff--Young inequality for Kahng's skew-matrix quantum groups; the optimal constant is strictly less than one for \(1<p<2\); at \(p=2\), Plancherel gives equality, and these quantum groups have no nonzero group-like projections with finite Haar weight.

title: Root vector localization and minimal nilpotent finite $W$-algebras
abstract:
Let \(\mathfrak{g}\) be any finite-dimensional complex simple Lie algebra, let $h^\vee$ be its dual Coxeter number, and let \(e\) be its highest-root vector which is a minimal nilpotent element. In this paper, using a result of Bavula on invariants of commuting locally nilpotent derivations, we show that \[
  U(\mathfrak{g})_f
  \cong \mathcal{D}^+_{h^\vee-2}\otimes \mathcal{D}_1\otimes U(\mathfrak{g},e), \]
  where the first factor is a polynomial Weyl algebra of rank $h^\vee-2$, the second factor is a Laurent Weyl algebra of rank one, and $U(\mathfrak{g},e)$ is the finite $W$-algebra associated with $\mathfrak{g}$ and $e$. As an application, we prove that if $M$ is a simple infinite-dimensional $\mathfrak{g}$-module with the minimal GK dimension on which $f-1$ acts locally nilpotently, then $M\cong P\otimes V$ for some simple $\mathcal{D}^+_{h^\vee-2}\otimes \mathcal{D}_1$-module $P$ and some finite-dimensional simple $U(\mathfrak{g},e)$-module $V$. We also give a new proof of the Skryabine quivalence and Petukhov's birational decomposition of the quotient division ring of $U(\mathfrak{g})$.

title: A Rankin-Selberg Integral for $SU_{2,2}$
abstract: We construct a Rankin-Selberg integral for the non-split quasi-split unitary group $SU_{2,2}$ and prove that it is Eulerian. We then compute the local integral at inert places where all data are unramified, and show that it represents the local adjoint $L$-function of $SU_{2,2}$.

title: Near-Optimal Complexity of Finding Approximate Local Minima of Nonconvex Finite Sums
abstract: We study the component-oracle complexity of finding approximate local minima of nonconvex finite sums under mean-squared averaged smoothness with parameter $L$ and a $ρ$-Lipschitz average Hessian. Each query returns the value, gradient, and one Hessian-vector product of a component. We show that the complexity in the high-accuracy regime $\varepsilon\le c_0L^2/(nρ)$ is $\tildeΘ(n^{3/4}L^{1/2}ρ^{1/4}Δ\varepsilon^{-7/4})$ for a sufficiently large initial gap $Δ$. We attain the upper bound by adapting the inverse solver and eigenvector routine of FastCubic to averaged smoothness. Our lower bound assigns the bridge edges of a nested chain to random components; a replicated spectral construction gives the same bound for unrestricted randomized algorithms. Under individual smoothness, a factor of $n^{1/4}$ remains for $\varepsilon\le cL^2/(n^2ρ)$, up to logarithmic factors. In the complementary low-accuracy regime, we propose PathVR, which uses $\tilde O(n+\sqrt{n}LΔ\varepsilon^{-2})$ queries and matches a lower bound from dense weak hiding.

title: Near linear mixing of random-cluster Glauber dynamics on random regular graphs
abstract:
We study the random-cluster model on locally treelike graphs at low temperatures. This is a model of dependent percolation parametrized by an edge probability $p \in (0,1)$ and a clustering weight $q \in [1,\infty)$, generalizing independent Bernoulli percolation ($q=1$) and closely related to the classical ferromagnetic Ising and Potts spin systems at integer $q$. For $q>2$, at parameter $p$ below the tree uniqueness threshold $p_{\mathsf u}(q,d)$, it is expected that sampling is easy and local Markov chains mix rapidly on all graphs with degree bounded by $d$. On typical graphs, the same is predicted at $p>p_{\mathsf s}(q,d)$, where $p_{\mathsf s}(q,d)$ is a second uniqueness transition point on the $d$-regular wired tree. Our result confirms this prediction for random regular graphs, showing that the random-cluster Glauber dynamics mix in time $O(n^{1+o(1)})$ on a random $d$-regular graph for all fixed $q>2$ and $p>p_{\mathsf s}$.
  For comparison, the best prior sampling results for these models that held for all $p>p_{\mathsf s}$ required $q\gtrsim \log d$ \cite{BGPZ26}. The key difficulty is that simply utilizing the contraction of cavity messages on $d$-regular trees does not suffice to cover the entire regime $q>2$. To address this issue, motivated by \cite{LS26}, we develop a careful bootstrap argument to show the shrinkage of disagreement under grand coupling. The core ideas of the proof were generated using GPT-6 and the Pharos system; the proof was then refined and simplified by the author.

title: Continuity and Stability of the FitzHugh Nagumo System with Respect to the Diffusion
abstract: Spatial heterogeneity in diffusion is a fundamental feature of excitable media, yet its effect on FitzHugh Nagumo dynamics remains mathematically challenging. We establish stability of solutions with respect to perturbations of the diffusion coefficient, providing a rigorous account of how changes in the medium affect the evolution of the system. Specifically, we prove a continuous dependence result ensuring that small perturbations in diffusion produce small variations in the corresponding solutions. The proof adapts the method of contracting rectangles to variable diffusion, yielding a framework for controlling and comparing solutions associated with different diffusion profiles. This result provides a rigorous link between heterogeneous and homogeneous FitzHugh Nagumo systems and justifies constant-diffusion approximations when the diffusion coefficient is close to a constant. Our analysis advances the understanding of FitzHugh Nagumo dynamics in heterogeneous media by establishing robustness with respect to spatial variations in diffusion.

title: Mixed-Integer Second-Order Cone Formulations for the Euclidean Bottleneck Steiner Tree Problem in $\mathbb{R}^d$
abstract: Given a set of terminals in $\mathbb{R}^d$ and an integer $k\ge0$, the Euclidean bottleneck Steiner tree problem (EBSTP) asks for a tree spanning the terminals with at most $k$ Steiner points that minimizes its longest edge. Although the planar case has been widely studied, exact optimization methods for arbitrary dimension remain scarce. We develop two exact mixed-integer second-order cone programming (MISOCP) formulations for the EBSTP: a single-commodity flow formulation and a formulation with connectivity cuts. Both formulations share a geometric core based on edge-conditional second-order cone constraints and are strengthened by problem-specific preprocessing, edge-dependent big-$M$ constants, symmetry-breaking constraints, constructive upper bounds, and new global lower bounds on the optimal value. We establish the correctness of the formulations and prove the validity of all strengthening techniques. Computational experiments on 1050 benchmark instances in dimensions $d\in\{2,3,4\}$, with up to $50$ terminals and $9$ Steiner points, show that the single-commodity flow formulation consistently outperforms the formulation with connectivity cuts, with an advantage { in solved instances} that grows with dimension. The proposed global lower bounds substantially strengthen the root relaxation, while the single-commodity flow formulation provides the most robust exact solution method across all test sets. These results establish the single-commodity flow formulation as an effective exact approach for the EBSTP in arbitrary fixed dimension.

title: Discrete Poincaré and Bogovskii operators for higher order finite element de Rham complexes
abstract: We present discrete Poincaré and Bogovskii operators for the common finite element discretizations of the de Rham complex of arbitrary polynomial order. We first discuss how such operators arise from a decomposition of the finite element spaces into a lowest order component and a remainder. This results in a fast algorithm for computing grad, curl, and div potentials. We then introduce a nonlocal Poincaré operator on contractible domains, which generalizes existing constructions based on cone operators to arbitrary order by integrating over cones against extended test forms. This requires developing commuting extension operators, which turn out to be related to rational forms. We also show how the nonlocal construction is modified to obtain a discrete Bogovskii operator preserving homogeneous boundary conditions. We further discuss how the ideas of the construction fit into the theory of finite element systems.

title: The Galois actions on braided fusion categories
abstract: This note harmonizes two classical topics: minimal modular extensions of braided fusion categories and the Galois action on modular fusion categories. Their common generalizations are Galois-modular extensions, which always exist when a braided fusion category $\mathcal{B}$ is pseudounitary. Each extension induces a Galois action on the simple objects of $\mathcal{B}$. Up to integral equivalence, the Galois-modular extensions of $\mathcal{B}$ form a torsor over an explicit group of homomorphisms from $\mathrm{Gal}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}/\mathbb{Q})$ to the invertible objects of order dividing two in the symmetric center $\mathcal{E}$ of $\mathcal{B}$. If $\mathcal{E}$ is Tannakian and $\mathcal{B}$ has a minimal modular extension, all minimal modular extensions induce one canonical Galois action. We prove that many facts about the modular data of modular fusion categories extend to pseudounitary premodular fusion categories as well via the Galois action.

title: Orthogonal polynomials on two or more intervals: the Sprugnoli context
abstract: We show how the group of Sprugnoli arrays on three elements can be used to define families of polynomials that are orthogonal on two intervals, and we indicate how the group can be extended in the hierarchy of Sprugnoli groups to yield families of orthogonal polynomials with more complex supports. In particular, we examine the defining three term recurrences and the Jacobi matrices of these families of orthogonal polynomials, while detailing the Sprugnoli matrix structure of the coefficient matrices of the polynomial families. We also consider integral representations of the principal moments on the defining intervals. Sprugnoli arrays are shown to relate to periodic recurrences where the parameters remain cyclically constant.

title: Calderón's complex interpolations of variable-exponent Fofana spaces
abstract: Fofana spaces, introduced in the framework of Wiener amalgam spaces, can be viewed as generalizations of Morrey spaces. These spaces have attracted considerable attention in recent years and have found applications in the study of partial differential equations. In this paper, we investigate their variable-exponent counterparts. More specifically, we describe Calderón's, first and second, complex interpolations of Fofana spaces with variable exponent, as well as the corresponding interpolation spaces of their preduals. Our results recover, as special cases, those already known for (classical) Fofana and Morrey spaces.

title: Stroh--Hamiltonian Framework for Modeling Incompressible Poroelastic Materials
abstract: The Stroh sextic formalism, developed by Stroh, offers a compelling framework for representing the equilibrium equations in anisotropic elasticity. This approach has proven particularly effective for studying multilayered structures and time-harmonic problems, owing to its ability to seamlessly integrate physical constraints into the analysis. By recognizing that the Stroh formalism aligns with the canonical Hamiltonian structure, this work extends its application to Biot's poroelasticity, focusing on scenarios where the solid material is incompressible and there is no fluid pressure gradient. The study introduces a novel Hamiltonian-based approach to analyze such systems, offering deeper insights into the interplay between solid incompressibility and fluid-solid coupling. A key novelty lies in the derivation of canonical equations under these constraints, enabling clearer interpretations of reversible poroelastic behavior. However, the framework assumes perfectly drained conditions and neglects dissipative effects, which limits its applicability to fully realistic scenarios involving energy loss or complex fluid dynamics. Despite this limitation, the work provides a foundational step toward understanding constrained poroelastic systems and paves the way for future extensions to more general cases, including dissipative and nonlinear regimes.

title: Generalized Disjunctive Programming with Derivative-Free Configuration Search
abstract: Generalized disjunctive programming (GDP) describes process design alternatives with Boolean variables, disjunctions, and logical propositions, and fixing one configuration leaves a subproblem in the continuous variables. Conventional GDP methods require explicit equations, which a simulator may not expose, and mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) reformulations can be intractable for nonconvex models. The external-variable reformulation turns configuration choice into an optimization over an integer lattice whose objective is the subproblem value, which derivative-free optimization (DFO) can search while the GDP model continues describing the alternatives. We pair GDP models with surrogate DFO methods and the direct-search method NOMAD and compare them with discrete steepest descent (D-SDA), logic-based and MINLP solvers, and enumeration on nine process models, 21 test functions, a pharmaceutical flowsheet simulated in PharmaPy, and a catalytic distillation column with 100,947 configurations. On the largest reactor network, the surrogate methods MISO and RBFOpt reach the reference in nine or ten of ten runs with about 30 subproblem solves, whereas logic-based methods solve nearly one subproblem for each admissible configuration and most D-SDA descents end at one local minimum. In the flowsheet example, where GDP solvers do not apply, RBFOpt and MISO find the best of 36 simulated configurations in every run with 20 evaluations. For the catalytic column, D-SDA and MISO reach the best known design with 100 evaluations, whereas MINLP solvers find no design within 15% of it and global solvers return contradictory certificates. This search pays off when the configuration space is too large to enumerate, has deceptive local minima, or has MINLP reformulations that fail, and enumeration or a direct reformulation is simpler for small algebraic models.

title: Extremal even-cycle-free subgraphs of the $k$-ary $n$-cube
abstract: A graph is said to be $H$-free if it contains no subgraph isomorphic to $H$. The generalized Turán number $\mathrm{ex}(G, H)$, a natural extension of the classical Turán number, is defined as the maximum number of edges in an $H$-free spanning subgraph of $G$. For any integer $\ell\geq 2$, let $C_{2\ell}$ denote the even cycle of length $2\ell$. So far, extensive studies of the generalized Turán number for the hypercube $Q_{n}$ have been conducted. The $k$-ary $n$-cube is an important family of graphs with many favorable properties, such as regularity and vertex-transitivity. It generalizes the hypercube and reduces to the hypercube when $k=2$. In this paper, we investigate the generalized Turán number $\mathrm{ex}(Q^{k}_{n}, C_{2\ell})$ of $Q^{k}_{n}$ for all even integers $k\geq 4$ and integers $\ell\geq 2$, generalizing the result for $Q_{n}$ [J. Graph Theory 16 (1992) 273-286] from $k=2$ to $k\geq 4$.

title: The Borodin--Kostochka inequality from degree 750
abstract: We prove that every finite simple graph $G$ with maximum degree at least $750$ satisfies $χ(G)\le\max\{ω(G),Δ(G)-1\}$. The proof starts with a random partial colouring and completes it on large cliques using a list-colouring condition that remains valid as the rest of the graph is coloured. Disjoint stars provide the required colours. We estimate the number of stars that can be chosen after the clique colours have been exposed, while keeping their endpoint set fixed. A common exponential-moment argument reduces intervals of packing sizes to endpoint comparisons. More detailed neighbourhood estimates handle the remaining vertices. The final probability inequalities are verified by directed rational and interval arithmetic.

title: Effect of a fourth-order diffusion term on the robustness of the transfer function stability for hyperbolic systems
abstract: We study a $2\times2$ hyperbolic system with anti-located control and observation. It is well known that the system can be stabilized with a delayed output-feedback control and that, unfortunately, this design is arbitrarily sensitive to small errors in the transport velocity. It was recently proved that adding a second-order diffusion term to the system restores robustness. We show that the same phenomenon occurs with a fourth-order diffusion term: the maximal spectral abscissa of the closed-loop system converges, as the diffusion parameter goes to zero, to the explicit value $-\ln(2)$, and the resulting stability margin is robust to small perturbations of the transport velocity. This additional term leads to a quartic characteristic equation whose roots have no tractable closed-form expression. We develop an asymptotic classification of its four roots and use it to obtain a first-order expansion of the transfer function with an explicit error bound. Combining this expansion with a topological degree argument, we show that $-\ln(2)$ is in fact the exact limiting value of the spectral abscissa, extending to the fourth-order case the sharpness result previously available only for second-order diffusive terms.

title: Rough-to-frozen transition in non-integrable dimer models
abstract: The transition from rough to frozen phases in models of random surfaces is expected to be governed by the Pokrovsky-Talapov law, which predicts a $\varepsilon^{3/2}$-type singularity of the macroscopic height profile (limit shape), as the distance $\varepsilon$ from the frozen phase (facet) is sent to zero. This has been proved so far only in exactly solvable cases, notably the classical, determinantal, 2D dimer model. In this paper we prove the validity of the Pokrovsky-Talapov law for a non-integrable 2D dimer model on the hexagonal lattice, whose Gibbs weight depends upon a weak plaquette interaction among dimers. Our proof is based on a multiscale analysis (constructive fermionic Renormalization Group), which allows us to identify two different regimes with distinct scaling properties and to explain the universality of the Pokrovsky-Talapov exponent $3/2$, in contrast with the interaction-dependent critical exponents characterizing the rough phase. The first regime, corresponding to smaller distances, is characterized by an effective quadratic dispersion relation, while the second comes with an effective linear dispersion relation, typical of Luttinger liquid behavior. As a byproduct of our construction, we control the scaling limit of the interacting dimer model uniformly in the distance from the frozen phase.

title: Construction, Enumeration and Duality of Perfectly Balanced Musical Sets of Order $2pq$
abstract: In this paper, we present a comprehensive study of perfectly balanced musical sets, also known in the literature as vanishing sums of roots of unity, in the particular case of order $2pq$. Starting from the well-established result concerning the decomposition of such sets as an integer linear combination of regular polygons, we first provide an algebraic formalization that allows to explicitly construct all these sets. We then propose six different decompositions of each set into regular polygons. Moreover, by investigating their combinatorial enumeration, we derive a formula for the exact number of these sets for a given order $2pq$, and describe their distribution and cardinality for the particular case of order $6p$. One of the main results concerns the duality that can be established between these sets. In particular, we prove that every non-periodic minimal perfectly balanced set of order $2pq$ can be combined with another one to produce a self-complementary $2p$-periodic set, and the reciprocal also holds. Finally, we demonstrate that the modulus of the discrete Fourier transform coefficients of dual sets are related. All these results shed new light on the distribution of perfectly balanced sets of order $2pq$ and suggest new mathematical questions in a more general case.

title: Boundary phenomena for slow recurrences:finite and infinite critical sets
abstract: For a second-order recurrence with positive integral coefficients, the slow length of an integer is the largest index at which it can occur when the initial terms range over positive integers. Spiro conjectured that, among a finite set of relatively prime recurrence pairs, a pair is slowest infinitely often precisely when its growth constant is strictly less than the square of the smallest growth constant. We study the equality case. For $T_m=\{(m-1,m),(m^2-1,m^2)\}$, the larger-growth pair attains the maximal slow length, with ties allowed, on $Θ_m(\log x)$ integers up to $x$ whenever $m\ge3$, whereas for $m=2$ its complete set of slowest integers is $\{1,2,25\}$. We give certificates for the infinite examples and prove a bounded-seed theorem that limits the possible initial pairs at each critical index.

title: Quartic polynomial differential systems with three disjoint invariant circles
abstract: We determine the normal forms of real planar polynomial differential systems of degree at most four with three prescribed pairwise disjoint invariant circles, covering all configurations of their centers. None of the prescribed circles is a limit cycle in the concentric case or in the coaxial case with three distinct centers, where the pairwise radical axes coincide. When exactly two centers coincide, or when the three centers are distinct and collinear and the circles are non-coaxial, we give necessary and sufficient conditions for all three circles to be algebraic limit cycles, which are necessarily hyperbolic. For non-collinear centers, we give explicit necessary and sufficient conditions for all three circles to be periodic orbits and for all three to be hyperbolic algebraic limit cycles. Each of the four configurations with non-collinear centers is realized by a coprime quartic polynomial differential system with three hyperbolic circular limit cycles.

title: Diophantine definability from addition and divisibility over rings of $S$-integers
abstract: Let $K$ be a number field, let $S$ be a finite set of places of $K$ containing the archimedean places, and let $\mathcal{O}_{K,S}$ denote the ring of $S$-integers of $K$. We prove that multiplication is positive-existentially definable in $(\mathcal{O}_{K,S},0,1,+,\mid)$ if and only if the unit group $\mathcal{O}_{K,S}^\times$ is infinite. This extends a 1977 theorem of Lipshitz for rings of integers to rings of $S$-integers. One of the key ingredients is a uniform bound for unit equations due to Evertse, Schlickewei and Schmidt, which we use to recover multiplication on the unit group.

title: Orbit Transversality for Projective Space
abstract: Let $f\colon \mathbb{P}^n\to \mathbb{P}^n$ be a dominant endomorphism defined over a number field $K$. We show that there is a finite extension $L/K$ such that every proper closed subset of $\mathbb{P}^n$ misses at least one grand $(f,L)$-orbit. Equivalently, $(\mathbb{P}^n,f,K)$ is strongly dense orbit transversal (S-DOT): every set containing exactly one representative of each grand $(f,L)$-orbit is Zariski dense in $\mathbb{P}^n$.

title: A motivic Vojta inequality for non-CM elliptic curves with unbounded height
abstract: We study a bounded-degree form of a motivic Vojta inequality for pure André motives, arising from a question of Kato. We verify this inequality for infinitely many non-CM elliptic curves with unbounded stable Faltings height. The point is that ramification at the finite poles of the $j$-invariant gives the required discriminant bound.

title: Infinitary real-valued logic and a refinement of the Kochen-Specker theorem
abstract: For nearly sixty years, refinements of the Bell-Kochen-Specker theorem have concentrated on finite configurations, combinatorics and robustness; once a configuration is fixed, contextuality is witnessed by the inconsistency of a finite family of Boolean constraints. We study the theorem instead with infinitary real-valued logic and a model existence game. We axiomatize, in real-valued $L_{ω_1ω}$, the lattice of closed subspaces of a separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space together with a quantum probability measure. In the standard models the theory recovers Gleason's theorem. Once the axiom that the measure is $\{0,1\}$-valued is adjoined, the theory has no models, standard or nonstandard, although every finite set of its axioms has one; a model existence game converts this infinitary inconsistency into finite inconsistent sets of interval commitments on the values of sentences. Over the standard models, the subsets of $[0,1]$ that formulas define through the values of the measure are exactly the $σ$-projective sets, the members of the least class containing the Borel sets and closed under complements, countable unions and projections along $\mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}$; the classification is proved in ZFC. For a specified strategy in the game, the plays that complete the parity argument for the eighteen-ray configuration of Cabello, Estebaranz and García-Alcaine record the geometric identities between the occurrences of a ray in different contexts, and the use that the measure makes of them. Probabilities are tracked up to rational tolerances, and $σ$-additivity along a named basis selects the four-dimensional block in which the argument takes place. The refinement is thus not a smaller Kochen-Specker set but a finer analysis of the logical form of the obstruction.

title: A liquid vapor phase transition in quantum statistical mechanics
abstract: We prove a liquid vapor phase transition for a quantum system of particles in the continuum. The system is the quantum version with Boltzmann statistics of the point particles model introduced in by Lebowitz, Mazel and Presutti.

title: Linear-length cycles in the supercritical percolated hypercube
abstract: Let $Q_p^d$ be the random subgraph of the $d$-dimensional binary hypercube obtained by retaining each edge independently with probability $p$. A long-standing folklore conjecture states that the emergence of the giant component in $Q_p^d$, at $p\approx 1/d$, is accompanied by the emergence of cycles of linear length. We confirm this conjecture and determine the order of the longest cycle near the phase transition. Specifically, for every sufficiently small constant $\varepsilon>0$, we show that if $p=(1+\varepsilon)/d$, then with high probability the longest cycle of $Q_p^d$ has length $Θ(\varepsilon^2 2^d)$. The dependence on $\varepsilon$ is optimal up to constant factors.

title: Conjugator length of Bestvina-Brady groups
abstract: We classify the conjugator length functions of Bestvina-Brady groups. We show that the conjugator length function, when non-trivial, grows as a linear or quadratic polynomial. In fact, we give explicit criteria on the defining graph to determine the precise degree of the polynomial. The proof generalises ideas of Bridson, Riley, and Sale by exploiting the framework developed by Chang and the authors to classify the Dehn functions of Bestvina-Brady groups.

title: IC-rigidity and generalizations of a theorem of Mahler
abstract: Mahler showed that for every irrational $α$ and every base ${b\geq 2}$, there is a single positive integer $n$ such that every digit in $\{0, \dots, b-1\}$ occurs infinitely often in the base-$b$ expansion of $nα$. Furstenberg later observed that dynamical methods can be used to give a different proof. Building on this perspective, we give generalizations of Mahler's theorem in two directions: the multipliers are a syndetic subset of certain multiplicative semigroups, and analogous versions hold in higher dimensions. Our main tool is IC-rigidity, a type of rigidity which is a hybrid of topological and measurable constraints.

title: When light travels with infinite speed: the electromagnetic loop circuits
abstract: Considering the ideal limit where the speed of light is infinite, or more precisely where the permittivity and permeability of the vaccuum are both zero, we construct a new type of electromagnetic circuit that we name an EM-loop circuit. These consist of wires having very high permittivity (E-wires) and wires having very high permeability (M-wires). These are threaded together by coils, the E-wire loops and M-wire loops. Some of the loops are terminal loops, pierced by an applied magnetic flux (for E-wire loops) or an applied displacement field (for M-wire loops) that are outside the vacuum since it does not support these fields. The response is the net flux of displacement field through a cross section of each E-wire terminal loop and the net magnetic flux through a cross section of each terminal M-wire loop. To calculate this response, the fields at the internal loops (those that are not terminal loops) are eliminated from the equations.It turns out that the response is governed by a new class of function pairs - dual Herglotz functions. Superpositions of a special class of EM-loop circuits, termed fundamental, allow us to realize any pair of dual Herglotz functions. Thus, we have obtained a complete characterization of the response functions of EM-loop circuits.

title: Shotgun Assembly of the Non-Uniform Labeled Lattice Model
abstract: In this paper, we study the graph shotgun assembly problem in the labeled lattice model, as introduced by Mossel and Ross (2019). We start with a $d$-dimensional lattice of length $n$, where the color of each vertex is sampled i.i.d. from a distribution $π$. Then, we ask whether it is possible to reconstruct the coloring of the lattice given the coloring of each subgrid of length $k$. While previous work by Ding and Liu (2023) and Demidovich, Panichkin, and Zhukovskii (2023) identified the reconstruction threshold when $π$ is uniform, we examine the non-uniform case. This paper establishes a sufficient condition for the impossibility of reconstruction for $d \geq 2$ using information-theoretic arguments. Our negative result matches the known threshold in the uniform case.

title: Tight Lower Bounds under Matched High-Order Hölder Smoothness and Uniform Convexity
abstract: In this paper, we provide tight lower bounds for minimizing high-order Hölder-smooth and uniformly convex functions when their orders match. Specifically, we consider functions whose $p^{th}$-order derivatives are Hölder continuous with degree $ν$ and parameter $H$, and that are uniformly convex with degree $q$ and parameter $σ$. When these orders match, namely, $q = p + ν$, we show that any deterministic algorithm with access to derivatives up to order $p$ requires $Ω\left(\left(\frac{H}σ\right)^{\frac{2}{3(p+ν)-2}}\log\frac{Δ_0}ε\right)$ oracle calls to reduce an initial optimality gap of $Δ_0$ to $ε$. This matches the corresponding upper bound and establishes a higher-order uniformly convex counterpart to Nesterov's classical first-order lower bound for strongly convex functions. Rather than directly generalizing Nesterov's classical quadratic-chain construction, we develop a multiscale phase-wise construction that preserves previous oracle responses while maintaining global Hölder smoothness and uniform convexity. Our result resolves the matched case left open by existing lower bounds for the two asymmetric regimes.

title: Filling Lipschitz spheres in metric spaces
abstract: We prove a homotopical Euclidean isoperimetric inequality for Lipschitz maps from the unit n-sphere into metric spaces admitting a bounded bicombing, which includes CAT(0)-spaces and normed vector spaces. To do so, we first refine the second-named author's Euclidean isoperimetric inequality for singular Lipschitz chains to this setting. Then, we show that a singular Lipschitz chain filling induces a Lipschitz map filling of almost the same volume or less, by adapting a strategy seen in work of Gromov and others.

title: A topological Mundici representation theorem
abstract: We lift Mundici's equivalence between MV-algebras and abelian $\ell$-groups with a strong unit to the topological setting. To this end, we prove that, for every topological MV-algebra, the associated Mundici group can be endowed with a topology that extends the topology of the MV-algebra and makes it into an abelian topological $\ell$-group. Among such topologies there is a finest one; we identify this topology as the topological-group reflection of the bounded-stage final topology, and construct an explicit zero-neighbourhood base in terms of the original MV-algebra topology. Using this topology, we establish a topological Mundici adjunction that restricts to an equivalence between topological MV-algebras and Mundici-fine abelian topological $\ell$-groups with a strong unit. Here, Mundici-fine means that the group topology is the finest $\ell$-group extension of its unit-interval topology. We also identify extremal $\ell$-group extensions under additional hypotheses, and establish a quasitopological correspondence clarifying the distinction between separate and joint continuity.

title: On the existence of nonadmissible irreducible smooth representations of $p$-adic $\mathrm{GL}_n$
abstract: Let $p>7$ be a prime, let $n>1$, and let $F$ be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic $p$ not equal to $\mathbb{Q}_p$. For every extension $E$ of the residue field of $F$, we construct an irreducible smooth $E$-representation of $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$ which is not admissible. When $E$ is countable, we also construct such representations without a central character and with nonscalar endomorphisms.

title: Maximal Unipotent Monodromy and $p$-adic Eigenvalue Formulas
abstract: We establish p-adic formulas for the eigenvalues of Frobenius in the case of the family of hyperkloosterman sums. The deformation equation in this case has maximal unipotent monodromy, and the interplay of Frobenius and the differential equation plays an important role in establishing p-adic analytic formulas for the eigenvalues.

title: BMV conjecture and positivity of spectral shift for relatively Schatten perturbations
abstract: We establish BMV-type results and prove the positivity-preserving property and uniqueness of support-normalized spectral shift functions of arbitrary order for semibounded operators with relatively Schatten-von Neumann perturbations. We also derive correlation inequalities in the relative Hilbert-Schmidt case. These results build on a new positivity-preserving property for the trace of a higher-order operator derivative along a relatively Schatten direction and are obtained using methods of multilinear operator integration and approximation.

title: A Complete Characterization of $q$-Ary $2$-Designs in Doubly-Extended Reed-Solomon Codes
abstract: Let $\mathcal{C}_k$ be the doubly-extended Reed--Solomon code with parameters $[q+1, k, q-k+2]_q$. We give a complete characterization of when its codewords of a fixed weight form $q$-ary 2-designs. The main ingredient is an exact criterion showing that the number of $r$-subsets of $\mathbb{F}_q^*$ with a prescribed product is independent of that product if and only if $\gcd(r, q-1)=1$. Applying this criterion to the minimum-weight codewords of $\mathcal{C}_k$, we prove that they form a $q$-ary 2-design if and only if $\gcd(k-1, q-1)=1$. We further establish a propagation result for MDS codes showing that the $q$-ary 2-design property at minimum weight implies the same property at every nonzero weight. Consequently, $\mathcal{C}_k$ holds $q$-ary 2-designs at all nonzero weights if and only if $\gcd(k-1, q-1)=1$.

title: Gaussian free field limit for the Airy$_β$ line ensemble
abstract: We prove that the centered height function of the Airy$_β$ line ensemble converges for each $β>0$, under rescaling of space and time variables, towards the Gaussian free field in the half-plane. The conformal structure for GFF involves the spatial change of coordinate $x\mapsto \sqrt{-x}$. The $β$--dependence is isolated in the field rescaling by $\sqrtβ$. For the proofs we study the asymptotic expansions of the moments of Laplace transforms of the Airy$_β$ line ensemble developed in our previous work with Xu.

title: Non-Pseudo-Arithmetic Hyperbolic 4-Manifolds
abstract:
We give three explicit finite-volume hyperbolic Coxeter lattices in dimension four whose adjoint trace fields are not totally real. They are the reflection groups of the Ma--Zheng polytopes $P_{11,6}$, $P_{11,7}$, $P_{11,8}$. The obstruction is contained in two cyclic products of the doubled unit-normal Gram matrix $A=2G$. Those products recover elements $s=\sqrt5$ and $u$ satisfying $$ (s-1)u^2+2(s-3)u+s-7=0. $$
  After the embedding $s\mapsto-\sqrt5$, this quadratic has discriminant $8(1-\sqrt5)<0$. The cyclic-product field therefore has a complex place. Vinberg's identification of that field with the adjoint trace field and the Emery--Mila total-reality obstruction imply that the three lattices are not pseudo-arithmetic. Torsion-free orientation-preserving finite-index subgroups yield orientable noncompact finite-volume hyperbolic $4$-manifolds with the same obstruction.
  Exact computations check the census data and provide independent field and finite-volume certificates. A pinned Lean~4 development verifies the radical identity and the number-field obstruction. It also checks the lattice and manifold implications conditional on explicit geometric and literature hypotheses.

title: Collision Parameters in Higher-Dimensional Families of Polynomials
abstract: Let $d\geq 3$ and consider the generic family of monic normalized polynomials $f_{\mathbf{t}}(z)=z^d+t_1z^{d-2}+t_2z^{d-3}+\cdots+t_{d-2}z+t_{d-1}$, where $\mathbf{t}=(t_1,\ldots,t_{d-1})$. Given pairwise distinct starting points $α_1,\ldots,α_d\in\bar{\mathbb{Q}}$ and a target point $β\in\bar{\mathbb{Q}}$, we show that the set of parameters $\boldsymbolλ\in\mathbb{A}^{d-1}(\bar{\mathbb{Q}})$ for which $β$ belongs to the forward orbit of every $α_i$ under $f_{\boldsymbolλ}$ is not Zariski dense in $\mathbb{A}^{d-1}$.

title: Translate, then decide: asymptotic optimality of latent-space control in bistable systems
abstract: This paper asks whether an optimal decision can be separated from the physical dynamics on which it acts. It studies this question through minimum-energy barrier crossing in scalar bistable systems. It characterizes the finite-horizon optimal feedback and shows that, as the horizon grows, it converges to a law that doubles and reverses the drift while it opposes crossing, and switches off once the barrier is passed. In physical coordinates, this law inherits the plant's nonlinearity, entangling decision and dynamics. We show that a plant-specific translation of state, input, and time maps every double well in the considered class to the same unit-rate linear world model, allowing a downstream decision stage to use a single plant-independent control primitive. This separation generally loses optimality at finite horizons because the translation does not preserve the physical control energy. Nevertheless, we prove that the excess physical energy of the layered controller vanishes as the horizon grows and that its limiting feedback reproduces the asymptotic optimum exactly. Thus, translation and optimization generally do not commute at a finite horizon, but commute in the asymptotic limit.

title: Weak and strong convergence of a general splitting approach for monotone multioperator inclusions
abstract: In this paper, we study a general forward-backward splitting approach for monotone inclusion problems that simultaneously accommodate set-valued, monotone Lipschitz continuous, and cocoercive operators. Weak convergence is established under a general setting. Strong convergence is obtained when both the maximally monotone operators are linear relations and the monotone Lipschitz continuous and cocoercive operators are linear. When the set-valued operators are normal cones to closed linear subspaces, we derive an explicit characterization of limit points of generated sequences using a new technique. Numerical experiments on a quadratic minimization problem with multiple-set split feasibility constraints are presented to illustrate the theoretical results.

title: On Fujita's Advanced Generalized Mukai Conjecture
abstract: We prove Fujita's advanced generalized Mukai conjecture for smooth complex Fano varieties. Our starting point is the existence of independent two-point Gromov--Witten correspondences. We show that there are finitely many unsplit families of rational curves whose chains connect $X$. We use these families to bound the anticanonical degrees throughout the successive minimal horizontal construction, so every family in that construction is unsplit. Fujita's contraction theorem and inductive classification then give the required list of varieties.

title: Isosceles sets in Euclidean spaces of dimension nine to twenty-two
abstract: A finite set of points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is isosceles if every three of its points form an isosceles triangle. Erdős asked in 1946 for the largest size $\mathrm{iso}(d)$ of an isosceles set in $\mathbb{R}^d$. The answer was known for $d\le 8$, the last cases being due to Ionin. We prove that $\mathrm{iso}(d)=\binom{d+1}{2}+1$ for $9\le d\le 21$ and $\mathrm{iso}(22)=276$, and that the extremal set is unique: for $d\le21$ it is the set of midpoints of the edges of a regular simplex together with its centroid, and for $d=22$ it is the McLaughlin configuration together with its centre. For $10\le d\le22$ every isosceles set with more than $\binom d2+3$ points is a two-distance set or a spherical two-distance set together with its centre, and the number $\binom d2+3$ is attained. The proof combines Blokhuis' decomposition of isosceles sets into mutually orthogonal two-distance sets, for which we give a short self-contained proof (the key step is a special case of Gallai's theorem on edge colourings without rainbow triangles), with the recent determination of the maximum two-distance sets in $\mathbb{R}^d$ for $9\le d\le22$ and with the known maximum sizes of spherical two-distance sets. In dimension nine this gives only $\mathrm{iso}(9)\le47$, and the exact value $46$ requires an additional argument about eight-dimensional two-distance sets with at least $44$ points. We also show that $\mathrm{iso}(23)=\max\{g(23),278\}$, where $g(23)$ is the largest size of a two-distance set in $\mathbb{R}^{23}$, so that $278\le\mathrm{iso}(23)\le575$.

title: Gromov hyperbolicity and uniformity
abstract:
In this paper, we first exhibit an example which answers negatively to a question posed by Herron et al. in 2008. That is, there is a rectifiably connected open set in a proper geodesic metric space so that it is Gromov hyperbolic with respect to the quasihyperbolic metric, and its Gromov boundary endowed with a visual metric is naturally bilipschitz equivalent to its metric boundary, but it is not uniform.
  Moreover, two positive answers are given under additional hypotheses. It is shown that a metric space is uniform if and only if it is Gromov hyperbolic and the natural map between its Gromov closure and its metric completion exists and satisfies a relatively quasisymmetric condition. Both bounded and unbounded cases are in our considerations via two different uniformization theorems developed recently by Bonk et al. and the first author, respectively. Finally, we characterize uniform metric spaces with uniformly perfect boundaries in terms of Gromov hyperbolicity and Teichmüller's displacement property.

title: Rule extensions of the implication--negation fragment of intuitionistic logic
abstract:
We present an algebraic study of extensions of the implication--negation fragment $\mathrm{IPC}_{	o,
eg}$ of intuitionistic propositional logic. Such extensions by inference rules correspond to subquasivarieties of the variety $\var{Ho}$ of Hilbert algebras with zero. We describe the lattice of such extensions of $\mathrm{IPC}_{	o,
eg}$ by means of its generators: it is isomorphic to the lattice of upsets of a countable poset, and in particular it is completely distributive. Consequently, $\var{Ho}$ is not Q-universal, in contrast to several other varieties related to $\mathrm{IPC}$. Nevertheless, this lattice is very complex: at each suitably defined height it has intervals containing continuum many quasivarieties which are not varieties. To the best of our knowledge $\mathrm{IPC}_{	o,
eg}$ is the only natural fragment of intuitionistic logic known to combine a completely distributive lattice of extensions with continuum many non-axiomatic extensions.

title: Occupation Measures in the ODE Method: Wasserstein Convergence and Rates
abstract: We study occupation measures associated with stochastic approximation recursions within the ordinary differential equation (ODE) method. Under Lyapunov conditions ensuring that the limiting ODE has a globally exponentially stable equilibrium, we establish that the continuous-time occupation measures associated with the piecewise linear interpolation of the iterates converge almost surely in the $2$-Wasserstein topology to the Dirac mass at the equilibrium, the unique invariant probability measure of the limiting semiflow. The choice of the $2$-Wasserstein distance is naturally aligned with our continuous- and discrete-time Lyapunov drift analysis. We also consider two discrete-time sequences of occupation measures, induced by the algorithmic time scale and the iteration count, respectively, and we establish their almost sure convergence to the same invariant measure in the $2$-Wasserstein distance. We then derive corresponding convergence rates in expectation, providing a nonasymptotic complement to the almost sure results. These expectation bounds also imply some tail probability estimates. Finally, we verify that our results apply to a canonical class of linear recursions.

title: Categorical Torelli and Fourier-Mukai partners of hypersurfaces
abstract: Let $X\subset\PP^{M-1}$ be a smooth hypersurface of degree $d<M$, and let $\Ku(X)$ be its Kuznetsov component, the orthogonal complement of the line bundles $\OO_X,\dots,\OO_X(M-d-1)$ in the derived category. We prove that $\Ku(X)$ determines $X$ for every smooth quartic in $\PP^{4k+1}$, $k\geq1$; together with earlier work, this gives categorical Torelli for every smooth hypersurface of degree $d<M$ with $d\nmid M$. The same algebraic reconstruction proves the classical generic Torelli theorem for these quartics, which completes generic Torelli for smooth hypersurfaces whose degree does not divide $M$, cubic surfaces excepted. When $d$ divides $M$, the Kuznetsov component is a Calabi--Yau category, as for cubic fourfolds, where categorical Torelli is known to fail. We show that, apart from cubic fourfolds, such a hypersurface has a number of Fourier--Mukai partners bounded by a constant depending only on $d$ and $M$, and that categorical Torelli holds in sufficiently large degree, in every dimension. The main tool is a deformation theorem: when geometric deformations surject onto the second Hochschild cohomology of the Kuznetsov components, an equivalence deforms together with the hypersurfaces, so statements proved for general hypersurfaces extend to all smooth ones.

title: Stable equivalence of quadratic monomial algebras
abstract: It is well known that gentle algebras are closed under derived equivalence. However, it is easy to verify that they are not closed under stable equivalence. We prove that the classes of quadratic monomial, almost gentle and string almost gentle algebras are closed under stable equivalence. In fact, in each of these cases, stable equivalence is characterized by isomorphism after deleting all nodes and removing semisimple direct summands. The underlying isomorphism theorem gives a positive answer to Martínez-Villa's question on selfinjective-free algebras for these classes. We also prove that the nonprojective simple modules form the unique weakly simple-minded system of a quadratic monomial algebra. Consequently, every stable equivalence of Morita type involving such an algebra lifts to a Morita equivalence when neither algebra has semisimple direct summands. Finally, we describe the effect of node deletion on stable categories of Gorenstein-projective modules and singularity categories, and give combinatorial descriptions of the equivalences for almost gentle algebras using marked configurations.

title: The Invocation Bottleneck in LLM-Based Lossless Compression: What Can Be Removed and What Must Be Traded
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) compress text far better than classical compressors, but LLM-based compressors are slow, particularly during decompression. We argue that their decoding time has two fundamentally different sources. Execution redundancy, such as per-token host transfers, CPU-side coding, and token-by-token encoding, is work that the coded output does not require and can be removed without changing a single output bit. Sequential dependency, one model call per decoded token, is inherent to lossless decoding and cannot be removed by better execution, only traded for more calls or for more bits. We remove execution redundancy with a GPU-resident pipeline whose block-parallel encoding is made lossless in half precision by batch-invariant kernels, speeding up arithmetic coding by up to 5.8x in encoding and 3.0x in decoding without changing its compression rate. We then study the two ways of trading sequential dependency, speculative dual-model coding (SDMC) and multi-token single-model coding (MSMC), characterize the compression cost of predicting several tokens from a shared prefix, and identify the workloads in which fewer model calls are worth that cost.

title: Cyclotomic factorization and fixed-point insertion in colored permutation groups
abstract: We extend cyclotomic Euler--Mahonian factorization to colored permutation groups for two inversion statistics: Biagioli--Zeng length and the inversion number of the underlying unsigned permutation. At a primitive $m$th root and rank $n=mk+i$, each normalized enumerator is a Hadamard product of a rank-$i$ colored enumerator and a weighted rank-$k$ type-B enumerator. Separate color variables are retained. The type-B factors agree for the two statistics, yielding equidistribution modulo the rank jointly with descent number, major index and negative-entry number. We also determine their exact changes under positive fixed-point insertion and obtain rational kernels retaining descent and major index. These kernels mark arbitrary fixed-point numbers and give derangement expansions at every inversion weight. Signed specializations recover type-A and type-B identities and give colored flag-major refinements. Inverse statistics and color-sum subgroups admit related insertion formulas.

title: Variational exponential estimates and stationary large deviations for SPDEs
abstract:
We establish an abstract criterion for large deviations of invariant measures when the deterministic dynamics has a single globally attracting equilibrium. Deterministic regularisation and attraction yield an endpoint estimate for long controlled paths of bounded action, uniformly over each fixed bounded initial set. This allows the finite time Freidlin-Wentzell uniform LDP on bounded initial sets to be combined directly with stationary exponential norm estimates. The proof requires neither a separate exponential tightness argument nor a Dembo-Zeitouni uniform LDP, and imposes no decay condition on differences between controlled trajectories. Finite path approximation identifies the quasipotential as the good rate function. We also establish a variational criterion based on the Boué-Dupuis representation that derives exponential estimates from bounds for controlled outputs, without requiring their convergence. Uniform controlled terminal moments yield estimates uniform in time, which pass to Krylov-Bogoliubov invariant measures.
  Together, these results establish stationary LDPs in four regimes: two-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations with possibly unbounded, globally Lipschitz, uniformly positive scalar amplitudes and vanishing noise correlation; reaction-diffusion systems without the additional restriction linking noise growth to reaction strength; Allen-Cahn equations with opposite boundary values and globally Lipschitz, uniformly nondegenerate multiplicative space-time white noise on intervals of arbitrary length; and Burgers equations with fixed covariance $(-Δ)^α$, $0\leqα<1/2$. For Burgers, we also obtain Gaussian norm estimates.

title: Observability and stabilizability for Grushin-Type parabolic equations in the whole space
abstract:
We study observability and stabilization for the whole-space Grushin heat equation $$ \partial_t u-Δ_γu=0,\qquad Δ_γ:=Δ_x+|x|^{2γ}Δ_y,\qquad (t,x,y)\in(0,T)\times\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^m,\quad γ>0. $$ For product sets $E=E_1\times E_2$, we identify three observability regimes in which thickness, distance from the degeneracy set $\{x=0\}$, and local density near that set play different roles.
  (i) In the subcritical regime $0<γ<1$, the observability inequality holds for every $T>0$ if and only if both $E_1$ and $E_2$ are thick; hence $T_{\min}(E)=0$.
  (ii) At the critical exponent $γ=1$, if $E_2=\mathbb{R}^m$ and $E_1\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is thick, we determine the exact minimal observable time: $$ T_{\min}(E)=\frac{a_{\mathrm{ess}}(E_1)^2}{2n},\qquad a_{\mathrm{ess}}(E_1):=\operatorname*{ess\,inf}_{x\in E_1}|x|. $$ Thus, the threshold depends on the essential distance of $E_1$ from the degeneracy set.
  (iii) In the supercritical regime $γ>1$, we consider $n=1$, $E_2=\mathbb{R}^m$ and thick sets $E_1\subset\mathbb{R}$. If $a_{\mathrm{ess}}(E_1)>0$, observability fails for every $T>0$, so that $T_{\min}(E)=+\infty$. If $a_{\mathrm{ess}}(E_1)=0$, observability depends on the density of $E_1$ near $0$, measured by $$ D_{E_1}(r):=\log\!\left(\frac{2r}{|E_1\cap(-r,r)|}\right),\qquad L_{E_1}:=\limsup_{r\downarrow0}r^2D_{E_1}(r). $$ If $L_{E_1}=0$, then $T_{\min}(E)=0$; if $0<L_{E_1}<\infty$, a finite sufficient observation time exists. Moreover, observability at time $T$ requires $$ \limsup_{r\downarrow0}r^{2(1+γ)/(γ-1)}D_{E_1}(r)\le C_{T,γ}. $$
  In contrast, for every $γ>0$, exponential and complete stabilizability hold if and only if both $E_1$ and $E_2$ are thick. The stabilization criterion is therefore independent of $γ$.

title: On rational curves relative to a divisor
abstract:
Let $X$ be a smooth complex projective variety and $D$ a reduced simple normal crossings divisor. We prove that, given a complete curve of negative $(K_X+D)$-degree, through its general points there is a rational curve whose normalization meets $D$ in at most one point. The proof uses ordinary weighted jets of a smooth family constructed from $(X,D)$, a positive parameter line bundle, and an intersection calculation on a ruled surface. We obtain an explicit degree bound depending on a projective embedding.
  We apply this construction to a cyclic cover compactification associated with a smooth Campana orbifold $(X,\sum_i(1-1/m_i)D_i)$. If its anticanonical divisor is big, we show that there is a covering family of free divisible Campana rational curves with fixed numerical class and contact data. In Picard number one case, the orbifold is Campana rationally connected.

title: Hotplug Coded Caching: Embedding the YMA and Interference Elimination Schemes via Reed--Muller Codes
abstract: In the hotplug coded caching model, $K$ users fill their caches of size $M$ as a function of $N$ files, but only an unknown subset of $A<K$ users is active in the delivery phase. We recently showed that (i) under uncoded placement, offline users cause a strict load penalty at intermediate memory sizes, so that coded placement is needed; and (ii) for $AM\leq N$, every classical scheme with row-wise placement, including the scheme of Gomez-Vilardebo (GV), can be embedded in a Reed-Solomon code, which removes the penalty. In this note, we show that every point of the scheme of Yu, Maddah-Ali and Avestimehr (YMA) for a classical system with $A$ users is achievable in the hotplug model for every $K\geq A$. Each user is associated with a hyperplane and each file with a homogeneous polynomial; each user caches the restriction of the polynomial to its hyperplane, and the subfiles seen by the active users are the values of the polynomial at the points where their hyperplanes meet. This is a projective Reed-Muller code, which reduces to the Reed-Solomon code when each subfile is cached by one user. We then show, by an existence argument, that every classical scheme whose cache is a linear compression of the Maddah-Ali-Niesen cache and whose correctness holds for generic coefficients can also be embedded over a sufficiently large field; this includes the interference elimination (IE) schemes of Tian and Chen. These embeddings complement the Reed-Solomon one, which allows any row-wise placement and any delivery. Together with past work, our results show that every point attained by a GV, YMA or IE scheme ($N\leq A$ for IE), and every corner point of the linear tradeoff for $A=N=3$, is achievable in the hotplug model with a load that does not depend on $K$. Whether the optimal hotplug tradeoff depends only on $A$ remains open, but these results support a positive answer.

title: Assouad--Nagata dimension of systolic complexes with almost flat intervals
abstract: We introduce the notion of systolic complexes with almost flat intervals. They constitute a subclass of fit systolic complexes and arise naturally in the study of graphical C(3)--T(6) small cancellation complexes. We prove that their Assouad--Nagata dimension is bounded above by a universal constant. As consequences, we obtain universal bounds on the Assouad--Nagata dimension of tame simply connected graphical C(3)--T(6) small cancellation complexes and of finitely generated groups defined by graphical C(3)--T(6) small cancellation presentations. In the appendix, we observe that the proof of finiteness of asymptotic dimension for buildings due to Dymara and Schick also yields finiteness of their asymptotic Assouad--Nagata dimension.

title: A toric approach to social choice theory
abstract: This paper initiates a systematic study of objects in convex geometry and toric algebraic geometry arising from status quo systems in social choice theory. Our main application is to classify all cones arising from a large class of status quo systems that are smooth or simplicial.

title: Conditions for Normality of Pontryagin's Maximum Principle in the Absence of State Constraints
abstract: Pontryagin's Maximum Principle is said to be "normal" for the problem at hand when it has a solution (maximizer u*) that explicitly involves the problem's cost function, making the maximum principle helpful (while in the opposite situation it is of no help). The aim of the present paper is, for Lagrange optimal control problems without state constraints, to identify classes of problems for which the Principle is normal. General conditions are introduced that guarantee normality, and classes of problems that satisfy these conditions are identified. Such classes include problems for which the constrained (by bounds on the control values) "augmented" reachable set, with cost along an upward vertical axis, has a convex lower-boundary function and the optimal terminal state lies in the relative interior of the reachable state set, with the terminal constraint within the affine hull of that set. Such classes include problems for which the constrained (by bounds on the values of the control signal) "augmented" (with the cost value along an upward "vertical axis") reachable set has a "convex" lower boundary for which the optimal terminal state lies in the relative interior of the set of reachable states. Special attention is given to Lagrange steering problems: sufficient conditions are obtained on a nested sequence of sub-classes of such problems, culminating with the class of steering problems with scalar control signal and linear time-invariant (LTI) state dynamics and objective integrand, for which normality is guaranteed whenever all eigenvalues of the state dynamics matrix A are real (e.g., if A is symmetric or triangular or the system is overdamped) or have small enough imaginary parts; simple 2 x 2 examples show that, in contrast with the situation in the finite-dimensional case, this property does not extend to arbitrary A matrices.

title: Exact signal recovery from generative priors with sigmoid output activation
abstract: We show exact signal recovery in generative compressed sensing for feedforward neural networks with piecewise-linear activations and a final sigmoid activation, with no assumption of expansivity. Consider a ReLU network of depth $d$ with a sigmoid final activation, whose input layer, of dimension $k$, is the narrowest, and let $K$ be the geometric mean of the widths of its layers. We show that, with high probability, all signals of the range whose entries lie in $[δ, 1 - δ]$ are uniformly recovered from $m \gtrsim k(d \log(K/k) + \log(1+\log(1/δ)))$ measurements.

title: Partitions with designated summands: $k$-tuples and their congruences
abstract: Let $A_k(n)$ and $B_k(n)$ be the numbers of ordered $k$-tuples of partitions with designated summands, respectively with designated summands and all parts odd, of total size $n$. Using an exact description of the generating function of designated partitions after a $3$-dissection, we classify for every $e$ the values of $k$ for which $A_k(3n+2)$ is divisible by $3^e$: this happens exactly when $k\equiv0$ or $-5\pmod{3^e}$ if $e\le4$, and when $3^e\mid k$ if $e\ge5$. We obtain the corresponding exact $3$-adic and several $2$-adic results for $B_k$ and for $A_k$ along the progressions $4n+3$, a recursion for the classes $3^b(3n+s)$, and for $k=2$ the congruences $A_2(12n+10)\equiv 27f_1^4f_6^3/f_2\pmod{81}$ in generating-function form. We relate the numbers $A_k(n)$ modulo $3$ and $9$ to overpartitions, sums of squares and triangular numbers, give group-action proofs of some of the congruences, and close with several conjectures supported by computation.

title: Pointfree convergence approach and pointfree index theory
abstract: Given a category $\mathsf{C}$ of lattices, we introduce the category $\mathsf{C^{Cap}}$, a pointfree version of the category $\Cap$ of convergence approach spaces, that contains $\Cap$ coreflectively, as well as the category $\mathsf{C^{Conv}}$, of pointfree convergence spaces introduced by Goubault-Larrecq and Mynard, both reflectively and coreflectively. We investigate pointfree counterparts of pseudo-approach, pre-approach, and approach spaces along two natural axes---depth and adherence-determinedness---which coincide in the spatial case but diverge in general lattices, and we determine when the point--powerset adjunction restricts to these subcategories. Unlike in $\mathsf{C^{Conv}}$, the category $\mathsf{Ap}$ of approach spaces finds a natural analog $\mathsf{C^{Ap}}$ in $\mathsf{C^{Cap}}$ and "index theory" translating traditional topological or metric results into generalizing inequalities can be conducted. We illustrate this with a result involving measure of continuity and measure of compactness.

title: Hamilton cycles in bicirculants with non-coprime connection sets
abstract:
A bicirculant is a regular graph that admits an automorphism having two vertex-orbits of the same size. A bicirculant can be described as follows. Given an integer $m \ge 1$ and sets $R, S, T \subseteq \mathbb{Z}_m$ such that $R=-R$, $T=-T$, $0 \not\in R \cup T$ and $0 \in S$, the graph $B(m;R,S,T)$ has vertex set $V=\{u_0,\dots,u_{m-1},v_0,\dots,v_{m-1}\}$ and edge set $E=\{u_iu_{i+j}| \ i \in \mathbb{Z}_m, j \in R\} \cup \{v_iv_{i+j}| \ i \in \mathbb{Z}_m, j \in T\} \cup \{u_iv_{i+j}| \ i \in \mathbb{Z}_m, j \in S\}.$ Some of the well known bicirculants include the generalized Petersen graphs and Cayley graphs of dihedral groups.
  In 1983, Brian Alspach proved that the only non-hamiltonian generalized Petersen graphs are $G(m,2)$ where $m \equiv 5 \pmod 6$. In a recent paper we conjectured that this is the only exception among regular connected bicirculants of degree at least two, and we have verified the conjecture for bicirculants with $|S|\le 3$. Results of Alspach, Chen and Dean imply that the conjecture also holds for all bicirculants with $m$ even and $\gcd(m,S)=1$. In this paper, we show that the conjecture holds for all bicirculants with $|S| \geq 4$ and $\gcd(m,S)>1$ such that $R\cup T$ contains an element that is not coprime to $\gcd(m,S)$ and, if $m$ is odd, is also not divisibile by $\gcd(m, S)$ or $R \cap T$ contains an element that is coprime to $\gcd(m,S)$.

title: On symmetry and monotonicity of singular solutions to critical fractional Hartree equations
abstract: This paper continues the study initiated in \cite{GuJevnikarYang2026b} of fractional Hartree equations with zero capacity singular sets. We are concerned here with the critical case, i.e. \[ (-Δ)^s u=\left(\int_{\mathbb{R}^N\setminusΓ} \frac{u^{2_{μ,s}^*}(y)}{|x-y|^μ}\,d y\right)u^{2_{μ,s}^*-1} \quad\text{in }\mathbb{R}^N\setminusΓ, \] where $N\ge2$, $s\in(0,1)$, $μ\in(0,N)$ and $2_{μ,s}^*$ is the critical exponent associated to this class of problems. We prove symmetry and monotonicity with respect to the singular set $Γ$. The Kelvin transforms centered at regular points provide sufficient decay at infinity for both the transformed solutions and their associated Hartree coefficients, without imposing global integrability assumptions. Combined with a moving plane argument and a comparison estimate in critical Lebesgue spaces, this allows the moving plane method to cover the full interaction range.

title: Low moments of sums of extended Rademacher random multiplicative functions
abstract:
Let $X^e \colon \mathbb{N} \to \{\pm 1\}$ be the random, completely multiplicative function whose values at the primes $(X^e(p))_{p \text{ prime}}$ are independent and uniformly distributed on $\{ \pm 1 \}$. Let $X=X^eμ^2$. We determine the order of magnitude of
  \[
  \mathbb{E} \Bigg[ \bigg| \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\sum_{n \le x} X^e(n) \bigg|^{2 q} \Bigg]\quad \text{ and }\quad \mathbb{E} \Bigg[ \bigg|\sum_{n \le x} \frac{X(n)}{\sqrt{n}} \bigg|^{2 q} \Bigg]
  \]
  for $q\in [0,1]$, showing that a transition from better-than-square-root cancellation to growth like a power of $\log x$ occurs when $q$ crosses $1/2$. In particular, the first absolute moments are of order $(\log\log x)^{3/4}$.
  The proof proceeds by comparing these sums to integrals of random Euler products, which are then studied by analogy with Gaussian multiplicative chaos integrals. The main difficulty lies in proving the lower bound at $q=1/2$, for which we also adapt arguments from the study of random walks.

title: Representation theory and massive spectral zeta functions on spherical space forms
abstract:
We study the spectral theory of the massive scalar kinetic operator on spherical space forms $Γ\backslash S^{3}$, where $Γ$ is a finite subgroup of $\mathrm{SO}(4)$ acting freely on $S^{3}$. Using the Peter-Weyl theorem and Molien series we compute the spectrum of the Laplace-Beltrami operator on $Γ\backslash S^3$ directly from representation theory, obtaining the eigenvalues and their multiplicities for all lens spaces $L(p,q)$ and for each ADE-class of finite subgroups of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$, which includes homogeneous lens spaces, prism spaces and quotients by the binary tetrahedral, octahedral and icosahedral groups, the last also known as the Poincaré homology sphere.
  For homogeneous quotients by subgroups of even order, we construct the meromorphic continuation of the spectral zeta function of the massive kinetic operator and obtain the general zeta-regularized determinant in closed form. The determinant is expressed as a finite sum of polylogarithms, valid for all real mass, and depends on $Γ$ only through its order and a finite set of parameters which we call twist coefficients fixed by the dimensions of the $Γ$-invariant subspaces.
  As a complementary approach, we express the heat trace of the kinetic operator on spherical space forms in terms of Jacobi theta functions, whose modular properties relate the spectral zeta function to geometric data, the volume and closed geodesic lengths of $Γ\backslash S^3$. We find that the spectral zeta function admits a rapidly convergent expansion in the heavy mass sector in terms of modified Bessel functions, and provides an independent check on the determinant.
  This framework extends to quotients of higher-dimensional manifolds directly, which we outline for future work.

title: Stabiliser codes over prime fields as weighted graphs and as quantum sets of lines
abstract: We further develop the theory of quantum stabiliser codes and its links with graph theory and finite geometry. We prove that an [[n,k,d]]_p stabiliser code over a finite field with p elements, p prime, gives rise to a graph on n-k vertices together with two disjoint independent sets of size k. Its edges are weighted with elements of a finite field of size p. If k=0, such codes are known as graph states. Second, we view stabiliser codes as so-called quantum sets of lines in projective space, allowing us to determined their minimum distance geometrically. We describe two geometrical operations to obtain new quantum sets of lines from given quantum sets of lines.
