abstract: We study natural exponential families whose generalized variance, the determinant of the covariance matrix, is log-affine in the natural parameter. Without any assumption on the natural parameter domain, we show that every such family is regular and that it is Gaussian when its generalized variance is constant. Consequently, a sample of size $n>d$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ comes from a non-degenerate normal law exactly when the conditional expectation of the sample generalized variance given the sample mean is a positive constant. Every non-Gaussian family puts mass on a facet of its convex support, and, as for a Poisson count, its height above that facet takes only integer multiples of a fixed step. More generally, its displacement away from any exposed face that carries mass has nonnegative integer coordinates in a suitable basis. A local inequality between third and fourth cumulants singles out the Poisson--Gaussian families and yields a complete classification of the infinitely divisible ones. Geometrically, a semi-flat Kähler tube, whose potential has constant Hessian determinant, is flat if some multiple of its metric is projectively induced near a point.

title: Sublinear multi-type preferential attachment
abstract: We consider a random growing graph model with two \emph{types}, or \emph{communities}, that belongs to the class of preferential attachment models. Starting from an initial graph $G_0$ in which each node has a type, the graph $G_{n+1}$ is generated by addition of a new node, which attaches through an edge to a node $v$ of $G_n$. The probability of attaching to $v$ depends on the communities of both the new node and $v$, and is proportional to $\operatorname{deg}_n(v)^γ$, where $γ\in[0, 1]$. We establish a convergence result for the limiting proportion of vertices of each degree and in each community in a certain regime of the parameter $γ$. To this end, we first use stochastic approximation techniques to reduce the convergence problem to the study of a non-linear evolution equation. We then use a probabilistic coupling approach to investigate the long-time behavior of the unique solution to this evolution equation. We emphasize that the techniques previously used to handle the single-community case cannot be extended directly to our setting. Indeed, the associated continuous-time embedding is not a multitype branching process in the usual sense, since the transition rates at any given time $t$ depend on the entire graph structure at that time.

title: Off-Diagonal Induced Ramsey Numbers
abstract: Given graphs $F$ and $H$, the induced Ramsey number $r_{\mathrm{ind}}(F,H)$ is the smallest integer $n$ for which there exists a graph $G$ on $n$ vertices such that every red-blue colouring of $E(G)$ contains either a blue induced copy of $F$ or a red induced copy of $H$. A conjecture of Kohayakawa, Prömel and Rödl asserts that, for every fixed graph $F$, this number is polynomial in $v(H)$. We prove this conjecture, showing that there is an absolute constant $C > 0$ such that $$r_{\mathrm{ind}}(F,H) \leq v(H)^{Cv(F)^2}$$ for all graphs $F$ and $H$. The proof combines a variant of a random geometric construction of Kohayakawa, Prömel and Rödl with the hypergraph container method.

title: $ω$-limit sets of triangular maps over periodic orbits of the base
abstract: Let $F(x,y)=(f(x),g(x,y))$ be a continuous triangular map of the unit square and let $z=(x_0,y_0)$ be a point such that $ω_f(x_0)$ is a periodic orbit $\{p_0,\dots,p_{m-1}\}$ of $f$. Then $ω_F(z)=\bigcup_{i}\{p_i\}\times M_i$ for nonempty compact sets $M_i$, and we ask which $m$-tuples $(M_0,\dots,M_{m-1})$ occur. For $m=1$ the answer is a theorem of Kolyada and Snoha. We show that a tuple occurs if and only if there are continuous surjections $M_i\to M_{i+1}$, indices modulo $m$, whose composition around the cycle is chain transitive. This is a cyclic version of classical facts due to Dowker and Friedlander, Sharkovsky, Hirsch, Smith and Zhao, and Kolyada and Snoha. It yields two necessary conditions: no $M_i$ is one of the exceptional sets of Kolyada and Snoha, and there are continuous surjections $M_0\to M_1\to\dots\to M_{m-1}\to M_0$. We prove that these conditions are also sufficient when every $M_i$ has uncountably many connected components, and when every $M_i$ has countably many components of which only finitely many are nondegenerate. In particular the sections of one $ω$-limit set need not be homeomorphic. Every tuple satisfying the two conditions falls into one of these cases or into a single remaining class, in which the sections have countably many components and infinitely many of them are nondegenerate; that class is studied in a companion paper.

title: The full Kolakoski shift is topologically transitive
abstract: We prove that the full Kolakoski shift---namely, the subshift of all smooth sequences over the alphabet $\{1,2\}$---is topologically transitive. Consequently, we demonstrate the existence of a smooth sequence whose factors are invariant under both reversal and bitwise complementation. As a further application, we prove the existence of arbitrarily long smooth words containing an equal number of occurrences of the symbols $1$ and $2$, providing evidence in support of Keane's conjecture. Our approach leverages the hierarchical structure of the full Kolakoski shift to reimagine the shift action in terms of a self-similar semigroup, which allows techniques from group theory and combinatorics to be applied.
